title: A Cell-Based Assay Optimized for High-Content Cilia Imaging with Primary Rat Hippocampal Neurons
protocol: Collect rat embryos to 10 cm dish containing 1× DM.
Peel away skin and skull using forceps under dissecting scope and collect brain.
Transfer brain to fresh 1× DM in 6 cm dish on ice, collect brain for each embryo.
Transfer brain to a fresh 1× DM in a 10 cm dish.
Grasp meninges from the brain with sterile forceps and gently pull them away.
Separate hemispheres from midbrain and hindbrain.
Isolate hippocampi and transfer them to a 6 cm dish on ice containing 5 mL of fresh 1× DM.
Add 25–30 units/mL papain to 10 mL solution of 3 mM L-Cysteine, mix well.
Place the mixed solution in a water bath at 37°C for a few minutes.
Transfer 5 mL of hippocampi to a 15 mL conical tube using a 10 mL pipette and let them settle to the bottom of the tube.
Filter sterilize papain/L-Cysteine with a 0.2 μm membrane into a 50 mL conical tube.
Remove 4 mL of 1× DM from hippocampi, add 5 mL papain/L-Cysteine, mix by inverting the tube.
Place the mixed solution in a water bath at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Filter sterilize 20 mL of trypsin inhibitor with a 0.2 μm membrane into a fresh 50 mL conical tube and place it in a water bath.
Remove papain/L-Cysteine from hippocampi using a 10 mL pipette, add 5 mL trypsin inhibitor, mix by inverting the tube.
Repeat three times with fresh trypsin inhibitor each time.
Remove last trypsin inhibitor wash.
Add 5 mL warm PM and gently triturate with a 10 mL pipette until all clumps have disappeared.
Add 5 mL warm PM to achieve a total volume of 10 mL.
Filter the hippocampal culture through a cell strainer with a pore size of 40 μm.
Dilute the culture 1:5 in PM (make 50 μL).
Aliquot 10 μL of 0.4% Trypan Blue solution to an Eppendorf tube.
Add 10 μL of diluted neurons, mix by pipetting up and down.
Incubate for 3 min.
Transfer 10 μL to a hemocytometer.
Count viable (clear) neurons under light microscope.
Do not count unhealthy (blue) neurons.
Count 4 squares on the hemocytometer.
Calculate the number of viable cells using the formula: [4 squares × 2 × 5]/400 = n × 10^6 neurons/mL.
Make three different neuronal dilutions for an accurate estimate of neuronal counts.
Dilute culture to 5 × 10^5 cells/mL with PM (make 6 mL).
Add 50 μL neuron culture to wells of 96 plate containing 80 μL of PM/well, gently mix by pipetting up/down.
Tap plate to homogenously disperse neurons in the wells.
Place plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Plate neurons at 25,000 per well in a 96-well plate for cilia imaging.
Use gentle pipetting when plating the neurons to avoid generating aerosol and causing cell damage.
Dissociated neuronal cultures can be stored on ice for up to 4-5 hours before plating.
Thaw LV particles in water bath.
Prepare a 1:1 dilution of LV in NB medium with polybrene at 0.6 μg/mL.
Transduce neurons by replacing PM medium with diluted virus at 70 μL/well in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
After 6 hours, wash neurons twice with NB-wash medium at 100 μL/well.
Replace the last wash with 130 μL of PM medium.
Change PM medium every 3–4 days; keep neurons in culture until DIV13.
De-contaminate labware that touched LV by soaking in 30% bleach for at least 20 minutes before discarding in biohazardous waste.
Set up a reservoir filled with 6 mL of ice-cold methanol on ice.
Prepare a reservoir containing 6 mL of 1× PBS and another with 6 mL of freshly thawed 4% PFA.
Transfer plate with neurons to chemical hood, replace PM medium with 4% PFA and incubate for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Replace fixative with 1× PBS.
Incubate plates with neurons expressing fluorescent proteins in a dark container.
Wrap plate with parafilm after fixation.
Store fixed neurons in 200 μL of 1× PBS with 0.05% Sodium Azide (NaN3) at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Transfer plate on ice and replace 1× PBS with ice-cold 100% MeOH.
Incubate plate with ice-cold MeOH for 10 minutes.
Invert plate to quickly remove MeOH and dry by tapping on clean tissue.
Incubate plate with PBT-glycine for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Wash plate twice with PBT-glycine.
Replace PBT-glycine with PBT-block solution.
Incubate plate with PBT-block solution for 90 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Prepare primary antibody solution using anti-rabbit-adenylyl cyclase III diluted 1:700 and anti-chicken-GFP diluted 1:1,000 in PBT-block (make 6 mL).
Replace PBT-block with the prepared antibody solution.
Wrap plate with parafilm and store at 4°C for 16–24 hours.
Wash neurons with PBT buffer three times for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Dilute anti-rabbit Alexa-647 and anti-chicken Alexa-488 fluorescently labeled secondary antibodies to 1:1,000 in PBT-Block to make a total of 6 mL.
Incubate neurons with the secondary antibody solution for 90 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Replace the secondary antibody mix with Hoechst dye diluted 1:5,000 in PBS.
Incubate for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Wash neurons three times with PBT buffer and two times with 1× PBS.
Replace the last wash with 200 μL of 1× PBS containing 0.02% sodium azide (NaN3).
Use the spot detector algorithm in HCS Studio Cell Analysis Software for object identification.
Draw a circular mask around nuclei using Hoechst staining.
Identify GFP+ spots within the nuclei mask area.
Draw a circular mask with a diameter of 32 μm from the nuclei ROI to identify ACIII+ spots.
Exclude objects at the border of the well during analysis.
Use Hoechst staining for focal plane acquisition of the well.
Adjust Z offset for optimal resolution of neurons and cilia at 485 nm and 647 nm, respectively.
